title: Chapter 2 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of Pages & Routing concepts!

questions.question: What does a file at `pages/products/shoes.js` map to?
questions.explanation: The folder structure `products/shoes.js` creates the nested route `/products/shoes`.

questions.question: Which file represents the homepage?
questions.explanation: `pages/index.js` is the root route `/`.

questions.question: If you have both `pages/blog.js` and `pages/blog/index.js`, which file will handle the `/blog` route?
questions.explanation: Exact file match (`blog.js`) takes precedence over the folder's `index.js`.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `Link` component?
options: To enable client-side navigation without a full page reload
questions.explanation: `Link` provides SPA-like transitions, preserving state and avoiding full browser refreshes.

questions.question: The `Link` component automatically prefetches the destination page in production.
questions.explanation: Yes, when a Link enters the viewport, Next.js prefetches the page's code in the background for fast navigation.

questions.question: Which prop disables the default scroll-to-top behavior in `Link`?
questions.explanation: Set `scroll={false}` to preserve the current scroll position.

questions.question: How do you navigate programmatically in Next.js?
options: Use the `useRouter` hook and call `push` or `replace`
questions.explanation: `useRouter` from `next/router` provides `push`, `replace`, `back` for imperative navigation.

questions.question: What is the difference between `router.push` and `router.replace`?
options: `push` adds a history entry, `replace` does not
questions.explanation: `push` adds to browser history (back button works), `replace` overwrites the current entry (no back).

questions.question: Where do you place a custom 404 page?
questions.explanation: Create `pages/404.js` – Next.js automatically uses it as the Not Found page.

questions.question: Which file is used for custom server error pages (like 500)?
questions.explanation: `pages/_error.js` is the general error boundary for all status codes, including 500.

questions.question: To navigate back to the previous page using the router, you call router._____().
questions.explanation: `router.back()` is equivalent to clicking the browser’s back button.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `passHref` prop on `Link`?
options: It forces the href to be passed to a custom child component
questions.explanation: When wrapping a custom component that is not an `<a>` tag, `passHref` ensures the child receives the `href` attribute.

questions.question: You can only use the `useRouter` hook inside page components.
questions.explanation: `useRouter` can be used in any component within the Next.js app, not just pages.

questions.question: What does the `prefetch` prop on `Link` do when set to `false`?
options: Prevents automatic prefetching of the linked page
Makes the link only work on the server
questions.explanation: `prefetch={false}` stops the automatic background prefetching, which can be useful for rarely visited pages.

questions.question: If you have a folder `pages/dashboard/` with only `index.js`, what is the route?
questions.explanation: `index.js` inside a folder becomes the root of that path segment, so `/dashboard`.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Next.js file‑system routing?
options: Automatic route generation from file names
Routes defined in a configuration file
questions.explanation: Next.js uses the file system, not a config file, to determine routes. (Dynamic routes will be covered later.)

questions.question: What happens if you visit a URL that doesn't have a corresponding page file and you haven't created a custom 404?
questions.explanation: Next.js has a default 404 page that appears when no custom `404.js` exists.

questions.question: The `Link` component can be used to navigate to external URLs like `https://google.com`.
questions.explanation: `Link` is designed for internal navigation. For external URLs, use a regular `<a>` tag. Using Link for external may not behave as expected.

questions.question: When using `router.push('/login')` after a logout, which method might be better to prevent returning to the dashboard?
questions.explanation: `router.replace` overwrites the current history entry so the user cannot go back to the protected page.

questions.question: The file `pages/_____` is the custom error page for server‑side errors like 500.
questions.explanation: `pages/_error.js` catches both server and client errors and receives a `statusCode` prop.
